question: $y$ is inversely proportional to $x^2$.
When $x$ is doubled, what happens to $y$?
trap: Square first: y depends on x², not x.

beats.say: Most students get this wrong. Y is inversely proportional to X squared. When X is doubled, what happens to Y?
Pause. What do you think the next step is?
Many say Y is halved. Inverse means opposite, so double becomes half.
But Y depends on X squared, not on X. So square first.
Write Y equals K over X squared. Put in two X. Two X, all squared, is four X squared.
So the new Y is one quarter of the old Y. Y is divided by four.

verify:
k, x = symbols('k x', positive=True)
y = k / x**2
ynew = k / (2 * x)**2
assert simplify(ynew / y) == Rational(1, 4)
assert simplify(ynew / y) != Rational(1, 2)   # not halved
assert expand((2 * x)**2) == 4 * x**2
assert simplify(ynew - k / (4 * x**2)) == 0

youtube.title: Double x, and y is… halved? (Inverse proportion trap)
youtube.description: y is inversely proportional to x². Double x, and y is NOT halved — it is divided by 4. Square first.
